title: Sequester-proofing: automated residency + tenant isolation evidence
creator: Avery Collins
description:
Goal: Build an automated evidence pipeline and UI/CLI workflows that produce tenant-level ‘isolation & residency’ attestations for Dedicated deployments. These attestations must demonstrate where tenant data resides (region and physical residency metadata), retention policy enforcement (object lifecycle, database TTLs, log retention), and runtime isolation controls (network ACLs, VPC peering, storage encryption and KMS key bindings).

Why: Customers in regulated industries (finance, healthcare, government) require auditable proof that their workloads were served within specified geographies, that retention policies were applied, and that tenant isolation controls were active at given points in time. Producing these artifacts manually is slow and error-prone; automation reduces audit friction and supports self-serve evidence provisioning.

Scope: Dedicated capacity only (reserved GPU pools), tenant-level attestations (one artifact per tenant per evidence window), evidence generation automation (on-demand and scheduled), secure storage of evidence with immutability and access logging, surface in Console + expose CLI/download endpoint for customers and internal auditors.
acceptance_criteria: Automated evidence generator produces a signed attest.json and PDF summarizing residency, retention, and isolation controls for a tenant for a given date; generated artifacts include timestamps and signing metadata.
Evidence artifacts are written to a WORM-backed S3 bucket (or equivalent) with object immutability and retention configured per policy and accessible to authorized roles only.
Console shows a tenant-level ‘Residency & Isolation’ view with the latest attestation and links to historical artifacts; download flows available for internal audit and customer exports.
Retention settings applied to storage and logs are validated by automated checks (examples: DB TTLs, object lifecycle rules, audit-log retention) and failures surface as incidents in the Console.
Nightly scheduled run generates artifacts for all active Dedicated tenants and publishes a summary report to the compliance dashboard; ad-hoc runs available via CLI and internal API.
Integration tests covering: correct region tagging, KMS key binding verification, network ACL snapshotting, and artifact signing; tests run in CI and as part of the release pipeline.
tasks: Design: finalize attestation schema (JSON canonical format + PDF rendering template)
Infra: provision evidence-bucket with immutability & audit logging; create service KMS key for signing
Runtime: add tenant residency metadata to runtime metadata service and expose read-only API
Collector: implement collector that snapshots network, storage, and retention config for a tenant
Signer: build attestation signing service that uses KMS to produce verifiable signatures
Storage: implement TTL + WORM lifecycle rules and ACLs for artifacts
Console: add UI panel and download button for tenant attestations
CLI/API: add 'redwood attestations generate' and 'redwood attestations list' commands
E2E: write tests that validate artifact contents and signature verification
Docs: onboarding guide for enterprise customers and runbook for on-call teams
technical_design:
Architecture overview: a scheduled job (and on-demand API) triggers the Attestation Collector which queries three sources: (1) runtime metadata service for node/region assignment and active model versions, (2) infra config APIs for storage lifecycle and KMS bindings, and (3) network inventory for VPC/subnet/ACL snapshots. The collector produces a normalized canonical JSON describing state. The Attestation Signer calls a dedicated KMS signing key and attaches signature metadata. Artifacts are stored in an evidence-bucket with object lock enabled and write-once lifecycle. A lightweight renderer converts canonical JSON into a human-readable PDF summary for auditors. Console and CLI integrate with the Attestation API to surface artifacts.

Key implementation notes: minimize privileged API surface; collector runs with least privilege; signer uses asymmetric keys with rotation policy; all service-to-service calls logged to audit export; artifacts include a deterministic fingerprint to detect tampering. Use existing audit export pipeline (ENG-7012) to surface generation events to Compliance Slack channel.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal pilot): run nightly attestation generation for 5 internal Dedicated tenants, validate artifacts, and exercise signature verification in CI. Phase 2 (beta customers): enable opt-in for 3 customers and collect feedback; expose download in Console. Phase 3 (general availability): enable scheduled generation for all Dedicated tenants and provide self-serve attestation history for 180 days; update billing/usage docs if applicable. Rollback: disable scheduled generator and revoke public download links; artifacts remain in evidence-bucket but access requires manual approval.
testing_plan: Unit tests for collector parsers; integration tests that spin up a mocked infra API, a mocked KMS, and validate signed artifacts; E2E run in staging toggling a test tenant to Dedicated. Add CI gate that fails the build if signature verification fails or if the attestation schema diverges. Create a small fuzz test that mutates collected JSON and verifies deterministic fingerprinting detects changes.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Collector accidentally exposes tenant data beyond intended scope. Mitigation: collector produces only metadata (no raw logs or user data) and runs with scoped credentials; code review and security scan required before deploy.
Risk: KMS key compromise. Mitigation: rotate keys, limit principal bindings, and require multi-person approval for key rotation; sign-only service runs in hardened environment.
Risk: Large number of tenants causes generation job to exceed time window. Mitigation: batch generation, shard by region, and fallback to on-demand generation for lower-priority tenants.
